text:
alex: Hey team — Alex here, starting on runtime this week. I'm trying to build from HEAD inside the devcontainer and hitting a few gremlins with CUDA libs + ptxas. Any quick pointers?

sam: Welcome Alex :wave: Can you paste the exact error and `nvidia-smi` from both host and container? Also what distro + docker runtime are you using?

alex: Container error when running the built binary: `error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory`
Host driver: `Driver Version: 525.85.12`
Inside container I mounted host libs and set `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64` but still same. I tried `sudo ln -s /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcuda.so.1 /usr/lib/libcuda.so.1` — binary runs further but then `ptxas` fails with `ptxas fatal : Value for --gpu-name=sm_80 is not valid` when running tests.

sam: ok a couple of things: 1) prefer nvidia-container-toolkit (`--gpus=all`) instead of bind-mounting libs. 2) ptxas error usually indicates the `ptxas` in PATH is from a different CUDA toolkit than the libcuda/driver. Run `which ptxas` and `ptxas --version` inside the container.

eli: +1 to Sam. We typically avoid symlinking host libcuda into container unless troubleshooting. If you do symlink, run `sudo ldconfig` afterwards. Also check `ldd` on the binary to confirm which libcuda it's pointing to: `ldd ./build/my_runtime | grep cuda`.

alex: `which ptxas` -> `/usr/local/cuda-11.4/bin/ptxas` (yikes, container had an older cuda leftover). `ptxas --version` prints CUDA 11.4. Host is 12.1. So mismatch.

natanael: That explains `sm_80` issue — newer ptxas flags (and architectures) are supported only in newer toolkits. Either upgrade the toolkit in the container to 12.1 or make sure the runtime compiles with a lower arch (`-gencode arch=compute_80,code=sm_80` vs older support). For fast fix: install matching CUDA toolkit package in the devcontainer image or bind-mount the correct `/usr/local/cuda-12.1` but ensure PATH/LD_LIBRARY_PATH point to it and run `hash -r` (shell cache).

rosie: Adding practical steps we put in the onboarding doc: 1) Use our devcontainer base `redwood/rt-dev:cuda-12.1` (if you started from a forked template you might have `cuda-11`), 2) run `docker run --gpus=all --rm nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi` to validate runtime, 3) if you must symlink, do `sudo ln -sf /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcuda.so.1 /usr/lib/libcuda.so.1 && sudo ldconfig`.

alex: Thanks — I'll switch the devcontainer base to `redwood/rt-dev:cuda-12.1` and re-run. Quick Q: where is that image spec? Dockerfile in repo or infra registry?

sam: image is in `infra/docker/runtime-dev/Dockerfile` in the mono-repo. If you need immediate patch, add a `setup_cuda.sh` step in your `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` that installs `/usr/local/cuda-12.1` PATH and sets `ENV PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.1/bin:$PATH`. We can PR a longer-lived fix.

alex: did the change — `ptxas` now reports CUDA 12.1, binary starts but unit tests hit `undefined symbol: cublasLtMatmul` on startup.

eli: `cublasLt` missing usually means you need `libcublasLt.so` in your LD path or the toolkit installed didn't include cuBLASLt. Check `ls /usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64/libcublasLt*`. If missing, your image might be `-base` instead of `-devel`. Use the `-devel` variant or install `libcublas-dev` from the distro package.

natanael: Another quick check: `ldd ./build/my_runtime | grep cublas` and `readelf -d ./build/my_runtime | grep NEEDED`. If the symbol is missing at runtime but present in the library, you might be linking to an older cublas at link time. Rebuild with the correct `-L/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64` and `-lcublasLt`.

alex: Rebuilt with `-L/usr/local/cuda-12.1/lib64 -lcublasLt` and now tests mostly pass. Huge thanks. One last ask: who should I DM for devcontainer image perms if I want to push a small fix?

rosie: Ping me or @eli for the PR; infra will review for registry creds. I can also add a quick snippet to the onboarding checklist so future newbies don't hit this.

infra-bot: Notice: registry redwood/rt-dev updated 6m ago (tags: cuda-12.1, cuda-12.1-deps).

alex: awesome, thanks everyone! I'll open a tiny PR to pin devcontainer to `cuda-12.1-deps` and add a short note to the onboarding doc. :rocket:

sam: welcome aboard again — happy debugging! :tada:
